(i) coagulase negative staphylococcus is the most common cause of infective endocarditis; (ii) coagulases negative staphyococci are difficult to type; (iii) the typing methods are useful in determining whether isolates are from the same patient, or not; (iv) the typing results can help in determining whether the infecting organisms are the same, or different.
coagulase negative staphylococcus (CNS) are a group of bacteria which are very common in hospital environments, are often resistant to antibiotics, and are difficult to identify.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
no one method is sufficient to confirm the relationship of different isolates from the same patient.
the use of a combination of methods is required to establish the relatedness of isolates.
the use of multiple typing methods may help to identify an organism as the cause of infection.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the typing of CNS isolates from a single patient should include more than one method.
the use of multiple typing methods is necessary to confirm the identity of a given strain of coagulose negative Staphylococcus.
